hed: Senate takes 2:15 p.m. cloture vote on Clarity Act after Democrats send overnight counteroffer
dek: The Senate is scheduled to vote at approximately 2:15 p.m. Eastern Tuesday on cloture on the motion to proceed to H.R. 3633, the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act — a 60-vote procedural step that would open floor debate, not enact the bill. Late Monday, after a meeting in Minority Leader Chuck Schumer’s office, Senate Democrats delivered a written counterproposal seeking tighter ethics limits, Blockchain Regulatory Certainty Act changes, and Ag-title adjustments. Republican sponsors Sens. Cynthia Lummis, Tim Scott, and John Boozman say their Sunday 635-page substitute already incorporates 126 Democratic-requested edits — including Trump-accepted ethics language and a Treasury stablecoin deposit-flight circuit breaker — and have rejected further talks before the vote. Republicans hold 53 seats, so at least seven Democrats or independents are needed if the GOP conference stays united.

cl.body: Decrypt’s Tuesday floor-test wrap, CNBC’s pre-vote write-through, and American Banker’s stablecoin-yield analysis frame Democrats and bank lobbies as still unsatisfied — Warner, Gallego, and Warnock say ethics text leaves enforcement gaps around the first family, Warren calls loopholes too wide, and eight banking trades including the ABA say the Treasury circuit breaker only kicks in after deposit flight — while Gillibrand has urged colleagues to vote to get on the bill and keep negotiating on the floor.

cr.body: Lummis’s office release of the final text, Decrypt’s quote of Senate Banking spokesperson Jeff Naft that Democrats “move the goalposts again” after 126 changes, and CoinGape’s report of Lummis aide Katie Warbinton saying Democrats “have not budged an inch” cast Tuesday cloture as a take-it-or-leave-it test of whether the chamber will even begin debate — with White House crypto adviser Patrick Witt calling remaining edits “punctuation” and Lummis saying “there’s nothing left to give.”
